content.comment_body: Hello forum, I've recently programmed a [product_name] [article_no] with a [product_name] [article_no] for a water filtration application. Everything functioned well except for displaying warning messages (activated with a simple bit on both the controller and the display). However, I could not transfer the program because it reported that text blocks lacked an output connection. I'm puzzled by this, and I need it fully working by Monday for final testing. Thanks in advance. Attached is a ladder diagram showing the text connection. P.S. I'm using [product_name] [version_no] for programming, and simulation mode works flawlessly.
Hello [user_name], Could you switch to Function blocks? That way you can add an output after the text block. Best regards, [user_name]

In a [product_name] program, every block must end with an output terminal, and the outputs need to be properly connected. The connection can be digital or analog—either to another block's input or via flags, outputs, or open connectors. Digital connections use flags, outputs, or open connectors; analog blocks use analog flags or outputs. There are a few exceptions—flags and outputs don't require this. Simulation mode doesn't enforce these rules, but to download the program to the device, proper output connections are necessary. In your scenario, simply link an open connector to the message text block. [IMAGE]

Good morning, Thank you both for your advice. I'll connect the outputs as shown in your explanation. I wasn't aware that text blocks needed an output—I'm glad the forum exists for issues like this. Thanks again, your help is much appreciated.
Hello [user_name], Thanks for your feedback and for voting.

In [product_name], all blocks except for outputs, flags, and open connectors need to be connected externally. This isn't required in simulation, but for transferring the program to real hardware, it is necessary. Blocks not used externally (such as text blocks) can connect to an open output, flag, or output. You can also use outputs not available on your hardware; for example, use Output Q16 as a flag. If not enough open outputs, flags, or outputs are free, you can use AND or OR blocks to combine outputs from several text blocks and connect them to an available flag. Use the F2 key on your PC for more information on programming errors.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users were confused because a project involving text blocks simulated correctly in [product_name] [version_no], but could not be downloaded to the hardware due to missing output connections. This reveals a gap in software guidance causing workflow interruptions when moving from simulation to actual devices. The community was essential in explaining these differences and in helping users resolve logic connection requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect software logic that works during simulation to also work when transferring to hardware. They look for clear, proactive error messages and guidance to avoid transfer issues. Quick and straightforward solutions for text block connections are desired.
